transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03 16:00 PST
Duration: ~74 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya (Helix ML), Ben (Infra), Sara (Security), Ravi (Research)

Auto-generated summary: quick technical triage on recent accuracy regressions after moving to INT8/GPTQ and AWQ experiments; focus on mixed-precision ablation, KV cache interaction with batching, and constraints for VPC/on-prem benchmarking. Decided next steps include Redwood-run benchmarks, sharing configs, and scheduling on-prem bench.

Topics: mixed-precision ablation, KV cache eviction/consistency, batching SLOs, quantization conversion pipelines (GPTQ/AWQ), FP8 tradeoffs, VPC firewall and KMS integration.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 60 to 75 minutes, lots to go through, Marcus will lead the ablation details.
[00:18] Marcus: Hi all. Quick agenda: first recapping the regression pattern you shared, then ablation hypothesis (layerwise precision, KV cache interactions), then what we can run in your VPC/on‑prem.
[00:32] Dr. Priya: Thanks. To recap from our side, after we tried the GPTQ INT8 build we saw a 3.7% hit on our clinical extraction F1 on the nightly eval, weirdly concentrated in long-context prompts.
[00:46] Ravi: yeah and some hallucination patterns increased subtly, especially when prefix has repeated patient metadata, things that hit the KV lookups.
[01:02] Ben: And from infra, latency was fine, actually improved slightly, but throughput dropped in our batcher when KV cache eviction was happening, it looks like cache misses were serialized.
[01:18] Marcus: OK so two axes — accuracy vs numeric precision and secondarily KV cache + batching interactions. For accuracy, we think two places: activation quantization in attention projection layers and layernorm scaling precision. For the KV issues, it might be how we flush/serialize KV cache across batched requests in your on‑prem runner.
[01:35] Aisha: I'll flag — there's also a difference between our hosted fallback path and on‑prem optimized kernels, so some diffs are expected.
[01:47] Dr. Priya: Right, and just to be explicit, we tried both GPTQ-derived INT8 and an AWQ run; AWQ had slightly better perplexity but still a delta vs FP16 baseline.
[02:03] Marcus: Got it. Can I ask for a specific failing prompt? even one or two would help us reproduce.
[02:12] Ravi: I'll drop 2-3 in the chat after this, one is long multi-turn with identical patient attributes repeated.
[02:21] Ben: Also relevant — our on‑prem nodes are A10G-class GPUs with a slightly older CUDA driver, the kernels may be falling back to slower paths for FP8 emulation.
[02:36] Marcus: That matters. Kernel selection + fused ops vary with driver. Suggest we capture the operator trace during the failing run. We can instrument without impacting latency much.
[02:50] Sara: From security — we need to ensure any trace capture does not leak PHI; what are you collecting?
[02:58] Marcus: Good call. We only need operator-level logs and aggregated KV hit/miss counters; we won't capture raw tokens. We'll scrub any PII before it leaves the VPC.
[03:12] Sara: OK that's acceptable, send the data handling doc.
[03:20] Aisha: Noted — next steps include sending SOC2 and KMS info.
[03:27] Marcus: Back to ablation. Two experiments we propose: (A) layerwise rollback from INT8 to FP16 for top-k transformer blocks to find sensitive layers; (B) mixed FP8/INT8 profiles where attention computation stays higher precision but MLPs are quantized.
[03:48] Dr. Priya: For (A) what's the expected runtime cost? if we keep half the layers FP16 is the throughput loss acceptable?
[03:58] Marcus: It depends on batching. In our tests, reverting attention and layernorm to FP16 recovered ~70–90% of the accuracy hit with a 15–25% latency penalty for token emission, but throughput at steady-state depended on how batching and KV cache were configured.
[04:20] Ben: Interesting. We're seeing that when the KV cache grows to >2GB, our batching scheduler stalls to wait for memory eviction which kills throughput. Is Redwood's runtime doing async eviction?
[04:33] Marcus: Our runtime supports async KV eviction, but in on‑prem builds you can hit sync ops if the allocator is under pressure or if the kernel path lacks async cuBlas Scratch buffers. We'll validate with a memory/cuda-memtrace.
[04:50] Ravi: Could the quantization change activation ranges and thus change cache hit/miss patterns? e.g., different tokenization because of small numerical differences?
[04:59] Marcus: Good point — quantization can shift logits slightly, leading to different top-1 tokens and therefore divergence in subsequent KV entries. That's a systemic amplification effect.
[05:11] Aisha: So we need both ablation and a set of deterministic trace experiments where we force same sampling to isolate numeric impact.
[05:22] Dr. Priya: We have a deterministic eval harness (temp=0) for nightly tests, can use that for the first pass.
[05:30] Marcus: Perfect. We'll run layer-by-layer rollback under deterministic decoding to measure purely numerical drift.
[05:39] Ben: On the batching side, could Redwood share the batching policy config to try matching your hosted defaults? our scheduler currently coalesces by tenant which introduces variable sequence lengths.
[05:52] Marcus: Yes, we'll share the profiler and a suggested batcher policy. We often batch by padded-length buckets and limit max wait to 12ms for low-latency workloads. For throughput experiments we can bump to 50ms.
[06:07] Ravi: Is there an existing tool to replay our real traffic into Redwood's on‑prem runner? we prefer not to send traffic to hosted for privacy.
[06:16] Marcus: We have a replay harness you can run inside your VPC that captures traces and replays them locally; we'll provide instructions.
[06:26] Aisha: Marcus, quick aside — we should also test AWQ conversion script differences, some of Helix's earlier runs used a third-party tool which may have used different block sizes.
[06:37] Marcus: Absolutely. AWQ group size and per-channel scales matter a lot. We'll send our recommended group size table and conversion flags.
[06:47] Dr. Priya: On FP8 — we were curious about FP8 hybrid: keeping matmuls in FP8 but accumulation in FP16, any caveats?
[06:57] Marcus: FP8 shows gains but is more sensitive to outlier activations; accumulation in FP16 helps. On A10G GPUs, FP8 emulation might be slower if hardware doesn't support the fast path; also, FP8 tends to require calibrated per-layer clipping, otherwise you get occasional large errors.
[07:18] Ben: That ties to our kernel/driver concern. If we do FP8 emulation we'll get higher variance in latency distribution, which security/regulatory teams sometimes flag.
[07:29] Sara: Right, SLOs must remain predictable. Any variance above 95th percentile +20% is a red flag for us.
[07:38] Marcus: Noted — for the on‑prem bench we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and unit cost delta.
[07:45] Ravi: For the regression bisect, do you recommend per-layer integer rescaling or per-channel?
[07:53] Marcus: Per-channel symmetric scales often give better accuracy for attention weights; activation quantization sometimes needs per-tensor with dynamic bias correction. We'll propose a layered plan.
[08:06] Dr. Priya: If we find a few critical layers, can Redwood build a mixed-precision snapshot we can run daily?
[08:14] Aisha: Yes — we can produce a pinned model version with the mixed-precision profile and a rollout plan for your CI.
[08:23] Ben: On networking — for on‑prem bench, how does the private control plane integrate? we prefer minimal egress.
[08:31] Marcus: Our private deployment option supports a control plane brokered via peered VPC endpoints; all model data and inference stays in your VPC. We only require metadata heartbeats; we can run fully air-gapped for the on‑prem package too.
[08:47] Sara: KMS question — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for model keys and logs?
[08:55] Aisha: Yes, we support customer KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for model artifacts; we'll attach the doc.
[09:03] Sara: Great, send SOC2 + KMS procedures.
[09:09] Marcus: We'll also confirm what telemetry we need to collect for the bench. Nothing PII.
[09:17] Dr. Priya: On evaluation metrics, aside from F1, we track hallucination rates via a token-level guard. Will your regression test include those?
[09:25] Marcus: We'll include the same metrics if you provide the harness; otherwise we'll run our standard BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity and the F1 targets you supplied.
[09:36] Ravi: I'll attach our evaluation harness and the 500 prompt set by EOD.
[09:43] Aisha: Excellent. A practical question — timeline for Redwood's benchmark run and shared configs?
[09:50] Marcus: We can start the automated suite tomorrow inside a hosted dark pool for a quick baseline, but for VPC/on‑prem we need the prompt set and trace capture; we can have a first ablation report by 12/07.
[10:03] Dr. Priya: That works. Also, can you include a comparison table showing per-token costs across FP16/INT8 (GPTQ)/AWQ/FP8?
[10:12] Aisha: Yes we'll include unit economics in the deliverables.
[10:18] Ben: One more infra detail — our on-prem scheduler currently uses 2 concurrent streams per GPU for multi‑tenant consolidation; if you need to change we can adjust.
[10:28] Marcus: For the bench, single-tenant strong scaling gives the cleanest signal; request Ben to provision single-tenant runs for the day.
[10:36] Ben: Will do.
[10:39] (brief cross talk)
[10:46] Aisha: To recap next steps: Redwood runs ablation + bench, shares quantization configs and AWQ flags, Helix shares prompts and provisions on‑prem infra, security review and docs exchange. We'll set the on‑prem bench week of 12/15 as tentative.
[10:58] Dr. Priya: Thanks, that sounds good. Any risks we should call out now?
[11:05] Marcus: Biggest risk is driver/kernel mismatch causing unexpected slower FP8 paths; second is amplification from minor logits diffs via KV cache divergence. We'll prioritize kernel trace and deterministic replay to isolate.
[11:18] Sara: From compliance, please avoid shipping traces containing any PHI out of our VPC; we need a signed DPIA if anything goes to EU.
[11:27] Aisha: We'll route everything per your policy and include a DPIA if required.
[11:33] Ravi: I'll send the failing prompt set and the two long-context cases after the call.
[11:39] Marcus: Great, we'll kick off the ablation tomorrow and aim to share an initial artifact by 12/07.
[11:46] Aisha: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and share the docs.
[11:52] Dr. Priya: Appreciate it.
[12:00] (meeting ends)

References/links mentioned: Redwood quant flags doc (internal): https://redwood.example/quant-flags (shared after call), on‑prem replay harness: github.com/redwood/replay-harness (internal), suggested deck: \"quant-ablation-plan.pdf\" (to be attached).
